chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr and Ali ibn Hadeed together, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of his companions, from one of the two (peace be upon them) that he said:
Regarding the tooth of a child, if a man strikes it so it falls out and then grows back, he said: 'There is no retaliation (qisas) upon him, and upon him is the compensation (arsh).'

Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'And Jameel was asked, 'How much is the compensation for the tooth of a child and for breaking the hand?' So he said: 'Something small, and I do not see anything definite regarding it.''

key_terms.قِصَاص: Retaliation or fixed blood-money for specific injuries

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for breaking a child's baby tooth in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, the Imam distinguishes between qisas (retaliation) and arsh (compensation) for injuries to deciduous teeth, noting that because they fall out and regrow, the injury is considered minor and does not warrant fixed retaliation. The scholars highlight that 'arsh' here is discretionary (muqaddar) rather than fixed (ma'lum), reflecting the practical reality that the loss of a temporary tooth causes less permanent damage than a permanent one. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of proportionality in diya, where compensation is calibrated to the actual harm and duration of the injury.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr and Ali Bin Hadeed both together, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>)
having said with regards to teeth of a child, the man having struck these, so they fall off, then they grow back: ‘There is no retaliation upon him, and upon him is (payment of) the compensation’.

Ali<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘And Jameel asked, ‘How much is the compensation regarding teeth of the child, and breaking a hand?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Something small, and I<sup>asws</sup> do not see anything definite with regards to it’.
